svg.text: BLUEPRINT 05: VECTOR LINE INTEGRALS, CONSERVATIVE FIELDS & POTENTIALS ENGINE
Circulation & Work int_C F . dl • Parameterized Paths • Exact Differentials dphi • Path Independence Quad

g.text: 1. LINE INTEGRALS & PATH PARAMETERIZATION
MATHEMATICAL FORMULATION OF LINE INTEGRAL
Evaluation of work done W or tangential circulation along space curve C from P to Q:
W = int_C F . dl = int_C ( F_x dx + F_y dy + F_z dz )
Scalar Form:
int_C |F| cos(theta) ds (Tangential component projection)
Parameter t:
int_t1^t2 [ F_x(t) x'(t) + F_y(t) y'(t) + F_z(t) z'(t) ] dt
Reversal Law:
int_(-C) F . dl = - int_C F . dl (Path orientation sensitive!)
CANONICAL PATH PARAMETERIZATION RECIPES
1. STRAIGHT LINE SEGMENT FROM P(x_1, y_1, z_1) TO Q(x_2, y_2, z_2):
r(t) = P + t (Q - P) = (1 - t) P + t Q, where t in [0, 1]
dx = (x_2 - x_1) dt, dy = (y_2 - y_1) dt, dz = (z_2 - z_1) dt
2. PARABOLIC ARC y = k x^2 (GATE 2020 NAT DRILL):
Set x = t, y = k t^2 ==> dx = dt, dy = 2 k t dt
Integral from x_1 to x_2: int_x1^x2 [ F_x(t, k t^2) + F_y(t, k t^2) (2 k t) ] dt
Trivial polynomial integration; eliminates transcendental variables.
3. CIRCULAR ARC x^2 + y^2 = R^2 IN X-Y PLANE:
x = R cos(theta), y = R sin(theta) ==> dx = -R sin(th) dth, dy = R cos(th) dth
Counterclockwise loop: theta in [0, 2pi] | Clockwise loop: theta in [2pi, 0]
Differential displacement: dl = R dtheta a_theta
SOLVED GATE 2020 NAT DRILL (SLIDE 238)
Vector field F = a_x y - a_y x. Find int_C F . dl along y = x^2 from (-1, 1) to (2, 4):
Step 1: F . dl = (y i - x j) . (dx i + dy j) = y dx - x dy
Step 2: Parameterize along y = x^2: x = t, y = t^2 => dx = dt, dy = 2t dt
Step 3: Substitute: y dx - x dy = (t^2)(dt) - (t)(2t dt) = t^2 dt - 2t^2 dt = -t^2 dt
Step 4: Limits on t (= x): from t = -1 to t = 2
GATE ANSWER: -3 (Confirmed Chalkboard Match!)
2. CONSERVATIVE FIELDS & THE EQUIVALENCE QUAD
THE 4 EQUIVALENT DEFINITIONS OF A CONSERVATIVE FIELD
1. DIFFERENTIAL CRITERION
curl(F) = grad x F = 0
dF_z/dy = dF_y/dz
dF_x/dz = dF_z/dx, dF_y/dx = dF_x/dy
2. SCALAR POTENTIAL CRITERION
F = grad(phi)
F_x = dphi/dx, F_y = dphi/dy
F_z = dphi/dz (Scalar Potential phi)
3. CLOSED LOOP CRITERION
oint_C F . dl = 0
Net circulation along ANY closed
curve in simply connected domain is zero.
4. PATH INDEPENDENCE CRITERION
int_A^B F . dl = phi(B) - phi(A)
Work depends ONLY on endpoints A & B;
independent of the chosen trajectory C.
The Fundamental Theorem for Line Integrals: Direct analog of Calculus FTC 1 int_a^b f'(x) dx = f(b) - f(a)!
SOLVED CHALKBOARD MASTER DRILL: PATH INDEPENDENCE (SLIDE 218)
Evaluate int_P1^P2 (y dx + x dy) from P_1(x_1, y_1) to P_2(x_2, y_2) along a semicircle path:
Semicircular Path C_1
Straight Path C_2
THE CONSERVATIVE INSIGHT:
Vector Field: F = y i + x j
curl(F) = (d(x)/dx - d(y)/dy) k = (1 - 1) k = 0
=> F is 100% CONSERVATIVE!
The semicircular geometry is a DISTRACTOR; work is path-free!
METHOD 1: EXACT DIFFERENTIAL (10 SECONDS)
Recognize that:
y dx + x dy = d( x y )
Scalar potential: phi(x, y) = x y
int_P1^P2 (y dx + x dy) = int_P1^P2 d(xy)
= x_2 y_2 - x_1 y_1 [DONE]
METHOD 2: DIRECT PARAMETERIZATION (BRUTE)
Integrate from t = 0 to 1:
int_0^1 [ (t dy_0 + y_1) dx_0 + (t dx_0 + x_1) dy_0 ] dt
= x_2 y_2 - x_1 y_1 (Identical!)
Exam Takeaway: Always test curl F = 0 FIRST. If curl = 0, find potential phi and subtract endpoints in seconds!
3. POTENTIAL RECOVERY & CLOSED LOOP DYNAMICS
STEP-BY-STEP SCALAR POTENTIAL RECOVERY
STEP 1: PARTIAL INTEGRATION W.R.T. x
phi(x, y, z) = int F_x dx + g(y, z)
Here g(y, z) serves as the arbitrary integration function independent of x.
STEP 2: DIFFERENTIATE W.R.T. y & MATCH F_y
dphi/dy = d/dy [ int F_x dx ] + dg/dy == F_y
Isolates dg/dy and solves for g(y, z) = int [ ... ] dy + h(z).
STEP 3: DIFFERENTIATE W.R.T. z & MATCH F_z
dphi/dz == F_z ==> dh/dz == const ==> phi(x, y, z) IS COMPLETE!
Guaranteed single unique scalar function up to an additive constant C.
CLOSED LOOP LINE INTEGRALS: oint_C F . dl
THE CLOSED CONTOUR WORK THEOREM:
Case 1: F is Conservative (curl F = 0) ==> oint_C F . dl == 0
Case 2: F is Non-Conservative (curl F != 0) ==> oint_C F . dl != 0
Conversion to Surface Integral via Stokes': oint_C F . dl = iint_S (grad x F) . dS
GATE CRITICAL PITFALL: NON-SIMPLE CONNECTED DOMAINS
Consider F = (-y i + x j) / (x^2 + y^2) in R^2 \ {(0,0)}:
1. curl(F) = 0 everywhere EXCEPT at the origin (0, 0)!
2. Along any loop encircling origin: oint_C F . dl = 2pi != 0 !
Stokes' Theorem requires domain to be simply connected without punctured singularities.
LINE INTEGRAL DECISION PROTOCOL FOR GATE
CHECK 1: IS THE PATH A CLOSED LOOP?
If YES => Immediately use Green's Theorem (2D) or Stokes' Theorem (3D)!
Avoid evaluating line segments individually.
CHECK 2: IS THE VECTOR FIELD CONSERVATIVE?
Test grad x F = 0. If zero => Integrate exact differential dphi; work = phi(B) - phi(A)!
Bypasses complex paths (parabolas, spirals, semicircles).
CHECK 3: NON-CONSERVATIVE & OPEN PATH?
Parameterize path explicitly r(t), substitute x(t), y(t), z(t) and dt, then integrate.
Or close the loop with a simple straight line and apply Green's Theorem!
